correctness.rationale: For each side, an interior orthogonal foot splits its radial angular gap into two positive \(\arccos(h/d)\) angles. Each \(\arccos(h/d)\) strictly increases in d>h, forcing comparisons of candidate radii to alternate; an odd cycle cannot close with strict alternating signs. In log-radii the Jacobian has exactly two positive-factor permutation products whose signs agree at odd order, so the analytic implicit-function assertion follows. A one-parameter rhombus family witnesses even-order failure. The included checker passed 2,500 perturbed odd-polygon tests and exact geometric benchmarks, but finite tests are auxiliary.

value.rationale: Recent literature explicitly identifies labelled vertex-ray and side-support reconstruction as an unresolved natural geometric measurement problem. This theorem resolves global injectivity for the entire odd-sided strict-foot subclass with arbitrary positive nonconstant support distances, not a fixed shape count or a renaming of an established inequality. It identifies an exact parity boundary through continuous even-order nonidentifiability and derives positive Jacobian determinant and local analytic stability. These results directly inform geometric tomography/reconstruction.
